_schema: Exemptions for check-firewall-membership.py --census (GOL-2572, GOL-2582).
AN EMPTY ALLOWLIST IS THE GOAL STATE. Every entry here is a box, a rule or a
database that the census would otherwise fail on: a droplet behind no cloud
firewall, a firewall that allows a SENSITIVE_PORTS port from the whole
internet, or a managed database cluster whose trusted sources are empty or
world-open. Adding one does not make the exposure safe -- it records that a
human looked, decided to accept it for now, and named the issue that will
close it.
Every entry MUST carry:
id       DO droplet id (number), firewall id (uuid) or database cluster id
(uuid) -- the stable key
name     live name at time of writing; a mismatch is reported, not fatal
issue    GOL-NNNN tracking the fix. Enforced by regex; no issue, no exemption.
expires  YYYY-MM-DD. PAST THIS DATE THE ENTRY STOPS SUPPRESSING AND BECOMES
A FINDING ITSELF, so a 'temporary' exposure cannot quietly become
permanent by nobody re-reading this file.
why      one line a reviewer can judge without opening the issue
open_databases is the third section (GOL-2582). A managed database's trusted
sources are a different API object (/v2/databases/{id}/firewall) and a
different Terraform resource from everything under /v2/firewalls, so no amount
of droplet-firewall coverage reaches them -- and on DO an EMPTY list is not
'closed', it means the cluster's public host answers for any source with the
password. A cluster that has since become CLEAN is reported too, so a stale
entry gets pruned rather than sitting here forever covering nothing. An
UNREADABLE cluster is NOT covered by an entry here: an exemption accepts a
KNOWN exposure, and that posture is unknown.
open_port_firewalls entries MAY also carry:
ports    [22, 5432] -- scope the exemption to the ports actually reviewed.
MUST be a list of numbers. Omitting it exempts EVERY sensitive port
on that firewall and is printed as UNSCOPED, because accepting a
dormant :22 should not silently pre-accept a 5432 added next week.
`ports` means nothing in the other two sections -- an uncovered
droplet exposes every port and a cluster exposes one -- so it is
validated wherever it appears but only consulted for firewalls.
80 and 443 are NOT in SENSITIVE_PORTS and need no entry here: they are
world-open by design on grove-prod-odoo-fw and grove-prod-blogs-fw. This file
is for exposures with an owner and an end date; a permanent one does not
belong in a mechanism built around `expires`.
